+# Incident Postmortem: High p99 Latency & Edge Client Request Jitter on booklogr-api
+
+## Root Cause
+Commit d045aa4 ("Order library list by shelf position") introduced a performance regression in the `GET /v1/books` endpoint in `api/routes/books.py`. It replaced database-level sorting and pagination (`books.order_by(...).paginate(...)`) with fetching all book records from the database (`books.all()`), performing accent normalization and shelf-position sorting in Python memory, and manually slicing the result set. This caused high query overhead and worker pool saturation in Gunicorn, leading to request queuing and driving p99 latency to ~5 seconds.
+
+## Evidence Used
+- Alertmanager alerts `EdgeClientRequestJitter` and `BooklogrApiLatencyP99High` firing for `booklogr-api`.
+- Prometheus metrics showing `path="/v1/books"` p99 latency spiking to 4.97s.
+- `git log` and `git show d045aa4` revealing `books.all()` in-memory sorting introduced in `api/routes/books.py`.
+
+## What Was Changed
+- Reverted the in-memory sorting logic in `api/routes/books.py` back to SQL-level ordering and pagination (`books.order_by(...)` and `books.paginate(...)`).
